vBRIEFInfo.description: Inbound agent-skill supply-chain security pattern complementing Agent Trap Defenses (#480).

narratives.Description: Directive-built projects consume skills, plugins, and MCP servers whose trust signals (stars, one-time scanner verdicts) are gameable or stale. This is the inbound complement to Agent Trap Defenses (#480) and outbound disclosure (#1700): structural controls for what skills an agent is given.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Create content/patterns/agent-skill-supply-chain.md with RFC2119 guidance: treat skills as software, vet linked targets, pin versions or hashes with re-vet on change, least privilege for fetched actions, controlled install sources not stars-as-proof; cross-link issues 480 and 1700. 2. Add a discoverability pointer in content/patterns/llm-app.md and REFERENCES.md as appropriate. 3. Append CHANGELOG.md Unreleased. 4. Verify the new pattern file exists and mentions pin and re-vet guidance.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer adding agent skills to a directive project, I want inbound supply-chain guidance that rejects signal-based trust, so that marketplace stars and one-time scans are not treated as lasting proof.

items.title: New patterns entry for skill supply chain

narrative.Acceptance: Given content/patterns/agent-skill-supply-chain.md exists, when an operator reads it, then pin/re-vet, vet-linked-targets, least-privilege, and controlled-source guidance are present with #480/#1700 cross-links.
Given the pattern lands, when REFERENCES or sibling pattern indexes are checked, then the new entry is discoverable; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] notes it.
